branza_it: In tech, customers judge a product by its first screen, not by its feature count.
IT companies seldom lose on code quality. They fade because nobody understands what they sell.
The technology behind “#company#” may be brilliant, but the customer will see it the way the interface shows it.
branza_handel: In retail, everything happens in the moment someone faces a shelf or a screen, and “#company#” gets a few seconds for it.
A shop that looks like a hundred others competes on price alone.
Buyers choose with their eyes before they read the price list, and that includes “#company#”.
branza_uslugi: Services sell on trust, and trust starts with how the company looks before anyone says a word.
Clients see neither your work nor your hours, only your materials, so they judge “#company#” by how it looks.
In services, competence has to be shown. Having it convinces nobody.
branza_produkcja: Manufacturers can make a flawless thing and hide it in packaging nobody notices.
Industrial firms often have an excellent product and a catalogue from the nineties.
Buyers check how “#company#” looks long before they read the technical specification.
branza_gastro: In food and hospitality people eat with their eyes, and the first impression at the door decides.
A guest picks a place by its photo, sign and menu before tasting anything from the kitchen of “#company#”.
Taste is a promise that must be made earlier, and the look of the brand makes it.
branza_inne: Whatever the industry, customers begin with an impression and only then ask about details.
The cards do not know your industry by name, but they know people, and people judge “#company#” by a first impression.
In every industry the company that is easy to remember wins.
etap_start: At the start everything is still cheap to fix, so solid brand foundations pay back many times.
A beginning is the time for a first impression, and there is only one chance to make it well.
A new company has no history yet, so its look speaks for it.
etap_rozwoj: Growth drags every makeshift fix into view: the logo from week one, the site glued together over a weekend and three different styles.
The company grows faster than its image, and that gap becomes clearer every month.
Growth brings customers who compare “#company#” with the competition, and they compare by looks.
etap_dojrzala: A mature company has a reputation, but a reputation without a refresh starts to smell of dust.
Years on the market are capital, provided the image says the same as the experience.
Companies with a history usually look older than they are.
etap_zmiana: When a company changes direction, customers must work out again who “#company#” is, and only a consistent new image helps with that.
A change is the moment when the old brand stops fitting and the new one does not exist yet.
Whoever changes direction and keeps the old image sends customers a mixed signal.
